claim: ChemSpacE provides a genuine external direction-learning baseline on the frozen MolecuLA interface.
The continuous probe gives more gradual local control and more candidates satisfying published similarity constraints.
ChemSpacE is slightly stronger for cLogP rank ordering but substantially more aggressive in decoder space.
Large unconstrained gains are entangled with seed/scaffold loss, decoder saturation, and SA deterioration.
MolecuLA is a better molecular optimizer than complete ChemSpacE-supported generative models.
SELFIES or RDKit validity establishes chemical plausibility.
The paired extreme-SVM comparison is a 400-oracle-call baseline; it ranks the full cached label pool.
The historical 50-seed registry is excluded from both learners but is not test-partition-only.
